work.summary: Ownership of the following core tasks:
work.name: Hitachi Energy Ltd.
work.position: Product Development Engineer, Defectivity, BiMOS FrontEnd
highlights: Inspection strategy: Further develop and refine the existing inspection strategy (inline and outgoing); develop and maintain the offline automatic defect classification (defect categorization, defect criticality definition, in-time reporting); support the implementation of essential tools such as the online automatic defect classification and inspection recipe management; foresee new incoming defects and execute their containment via risk assessments.

Defect management & enablement: Take full ownership of defectivity-related topics, including the defect catalogues for operators and engineers and the NMR (Nonconforming Material Review) portfolio; ensure these documents are regularly updated and maintained, and coordinate training sessions for both operators and engineers.

Data-driven quality, yield and cost initiatives: Optical yield monitoring: Perform regular optical yield monitoring and continuously improve the monitoring processes; maintain data acquisition, reporting and analysis tools; support the integration of new solutions as required. Optical yield improvement: Analyze and classify optical yield data to identify opportunities for sustainable improvements; lead and execute improvement projects; provide data analysis, classification and defectivity expertise to support projects led by product, process, and process integration engineers.

Quality & yield issue resolution: Resolve and analyze product quality and yield issues related to optical yield through systematic investigation — evaluating and ensuring the quality of inspection recipes by reviewing and validating improvements introduced by metrology engineers; analyzing and classifying optical defects and quality concerns from inline and outgoing inspections to identify process-related root causes; contributing defectivity expertise during quality processes (NMR, Risk Assessment, CAR(Corrective Action Request)); triggering and conducting NMR and CAR activities with relevant data analysis; supporting ECR (Engineering Change Request) activities and new tool qualifications with defectivity analysis; cultivating proactive implementation of corrective and preventive actions.

Projects: Optical Yield Improvement: Led the rollout of offline automated defect classification and reporting, reducing manual classification effort by 85%, shortening defect response times, improving fine-grained defect classification accuracy, and leading risk assessments for defect criticality. Identified key optical yield detractors, supported process teams in eliminating the root causes through data-driven analysis, and implemented containment strategies for remaining dominating non-critical and cosmetic defect categories.

work.summary: Subject: ”Attosecond time‐resolved absorption spectroscopy in the water window” to investigate light-matter interaction by means of ultrafast spectroscopy technique in atoms and small molecules in the gas and liquid phases. Main responsibilities encompassed:
work.name: Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule Zürich
highlights: Research in Ultrafast Spectroscopy and Attosecond Science.
Investigation of light-matter interaction by means of ultrafast spectroscopy technique in atoms and small molecules in the gas and liquid phases.
Design and end-to-end construction of the beamline for the attosecond time-resolved absorption spectroscopy of gases and liquids in the water window.
Design and setup of attosecond beamline accessories, including an X-ray generation station, and spatiotemporal metrology stations in the femtosecond and attosecond domains.
Daily use and maintenance of an amplified femtosecond state-of-art laser system.
Software engineering, Scientific Computing and Data Analysis (Python: scipy, lmfit, pandas, epics, h5py, matplotlib).
Application Development (PyQt5, Qt Creator, LabVIEW).
Source Control (git) / Documentation / Testing.
Management of laboratory equipment and assets.
Side note: Published papers are available upon request.
